Your Lordships be pleased to grant such other and further orders, as may be deemed fit and proper by this Hon'ble Court in the interest of justice."

2. Learned advocate for the applicant submitted that the F.I.R. in question had been lodged by him wherein it is clearly stated that the opponent no.3 herein had subjected the applicant to drug abuse and despite specific allegations made against her by the applicant, this Court had granted ad-interim relief in her favour.

The opponent nos.1 and 2 happen to be mother-in-law and father-in-law of the applicant and against them also, the applicant had made specific allegations in her F.I.R. to the effect that they were demanding dowry from the applicant.
This Court ought to have taken this aspect into consideration before granting interim relief in favour of the opponent nos.1 to 3 herein.
He submitted to allow the present application and vacate the interim relief granted in favour of the opponent nos.1 to 3.
Learned advocate for the opponent nos.1 to 3 was not present when the matter was taken up for hearing.
4. Learned Additional Public Prosecutor submitted that an appropriate order may be passed in the present petition.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/15728/2024 IA ORDER DATED: 27/11/2025 undefined 5.
Heard learned advocates for the respective parties.

6. The opponent no.1 to 3 herein have preferred Special Criminal Application No.15728 of 2024 inter-alia praying for quashing of F.I.R. lodged by the present applicant against them at Manavadar Police Station for the offences punishable under the provisions of Sections 498A, 323 and 114 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

The said application came up for hearing before this Court on 03.12.2024 and the Coordinate Bench of this Court had passed an order dated 03.12.2024 making following observations:-
Learned advocate Mr. Ratanpura submits that the petitioners are the father-in-law,
mother-in-law and sister- inlaw, who are falsely implicated in the offence in question by the complainant; and that they are residing separately from the complainant which is admitted position; and that marriage span is only three months; on bare reading of the FIR, no case as alleged is made out against the petitioners; and that the allegations made in the FIR are with a view to implicate entire family in the offences punishable under Sections 498A and others of the IPC.
Learned APP for the State submits that on bare reading of the FIR, prima facie case is made out and therefore, no interference be called out by this Court.
